interpretation: A single-vector late-layer Z channel can encode and causally control all task facets when the encoder receives an authoritative canonical goal specification.
The failure on rendered distractor-bearing goals is therefore primarily a goal-extraction and distribution-shift problem, not a fundamental channel-capacity failure.
Near-perfect reversed-order paraphrase substitution shows that the canonical representation is robust to requirement order in this diagnostic.

Canonical preprocessing is privileged semantic structure, so this result does not establish superiority over ordinary text prompting; it establishes that the latent channel is functionally sufficient once the goal has been extracted.
